rules.label: Control relations run between points
rules.comment: The control relations from the sequences (ba:drives, feedback, requires, resets, switches) link one point to another: a setpoint drives an output, a sensor feeds back to it. ba:requests ends on equipment instead and is checked on its own.

rules.label: A field controller is on a network
rules.comment: Every field controller of a riser talks on a trunk (ba:isOnNetwork to a ba:Field_Network). One with none can't be reached, or the riser was misread.

rules.label: controls runs from a controller to equipment
rules.comment: ba:controls says which unit a controller runs the logic for: a controller on one end, equipment on the other.

rules.label: Controlled HVAC equipment has points
rules.comment: An air handler, terminal unit, chiller, boiler or pump the BAS runs must show at least one point; with none, the unit is in the graph but invisible to monitoring.

rules.label: feeds runs between equipment
rules.comment: In this model brick:feeds is a medium flowing from one unit or plant to another (AHU to VAV, hot water plant to reheat VAV). A unit serving a room is ba:serves; a place is rec:locatedIn (knowledge_model/README.md, Modelling decisions). Both ends are equipment or a system (a plant).

rules.label: hasLocation points at a location
rules.comment: hasLocation places a unit in a floor, room or zone. The export writes it as rec:locatedIn, which Brick 1.4 declares equivalent to brick:hasLocation. Its end must be a location (rec:Space, which brick:Location is a subclass of).

rules.label: hasPoint runs from equipment to a point
rules.comment: brick:hasPoint is only meaningful from a unit (or system, or location) to a point: anything else is a misread grouping.

rules.label: isHostedBy points at one controller
rules.comment: ba:isHostedBy says which controller a point or schedule lives in. Its end must be a controller (brick:Controller, ba:Field_Controller, ba:Supervisory_Controller), and only one: a BACnet object lives in one device.

rules.label: Every node has a class
rules.comment: A node the graph holds must say what it is (a Brick, BA or rec: class). Without one, no rule, view or agent can use it.

rules.label: A point belongs to exactly one equipment
rules.comment: Every point is read from one piece of equipment (or system). None: the point is orphaned and can't be found from its unit. Two: the grouping disagrees with itself.

failing.label: EF-LAB-1-S
messages: The point is not on exactly one equipment.

failing.label: EF-LAB-2-S
messages: The point is not on exactly one equipment.

rules.label: serves runs from equipment to a location
rules.comment: ba:serves says a terminal unit's thermostat is in this room or zone (see ba_extension.ttl): equipment on one end, a location on the other.

rules.label: A temperature point has a temperature unit
rules.comment: Where a temperature sensor or setpoint has a unit (brick:hasUnit, a QUDT unit), it must be a temperature: °F, °C or K. A pressure or flow unit means the class or the unit was misread. A point with no unit is not checked here.

rules.label: A VAV has a zone temperature sensor
rules.comment: A VAV box controls to its zone's temperature: without a zone air temperature sensor among its points, its loop can't be monitored or diagnosed. Applies to every VAV subclass (RVAV).
